messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager fired — service=embedder-prod severity=P1 — multiple hosts reporting container restarts + GPU OOMs. Alert links: https://pager.redwood/incident/1785554321, runbook: https://confluence/redwood/ib-incident.

sam: saw this. rack-eu-3 showing a sudden spike in IB retransmits ~17:45 UTC. no CPU pressure but KV cache miss rate jumped.

maya: I'm oncall, taking it. hitting customers? any 5xx spikes?

jon: yes — frontend 502/504s in us-east & eu-west. proxy logs show an increase in cross-node RPC latency and timeouts. metric snippets: kvcache_evictions +420%, rpc_retries +300%.

kira: grepping serving logs: repeated entries like `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` right after `rdma: packet retransmit` errors. containers seem to crash after ~30s of retransmit storms.

sam: sounds like RDMA packetloss -> kvcache thrash -> memory spikes on GPU (lots of redos) -> OOMs. I'll pull net stats.

sam: quick check on node-12: `ibstat -i mlx5_0` shows link flaps; ethtool counters show RX errors increasing.

sam: commands I'm running:
```
# ib diagnostics
ssh ops@node-12 'ibstat -v && cat /sys/class/net/ib0/statistics/rx_errors && cat /sys/class/net/ib0/statistics/tx_errors'
# netprobe run (30s)
./tools/ib-netprobe --targets node-10,node-11,node-12 --duration 30s --concurrency 50
```

maya: good. jon, can you start traffic steering to dedicated-fallback pool (no cross-node kvcache) for the largest customers? we need to stop cross-node RPCs while infra investigates.

jon: on it — shifting 30% of traffic for top-10 tenants to fallback_pool now (canary). watching errorrate.

jon: canary looks better for those tenants, 5xx down ~80% within 2m. overall 5xx still noisy because not all traffic shifted.

maya: sam, try disabling cross-node kvcache in the runtime config for serving-1. This avoids KV fetch RPCs across IB.

sam: toggled runtime flag `--kvcache.cross_node=false` on pool serving-1 (hot reload). will watch evictions.

kira: after the toggle, I see kvcache_evictions start to stabilize. GPUs still show high memory churn on nodes that recently flapped.

infra-oncall: we pulled switch logs — multiple ports on TOR-34 hit ECN/backpressure surge and retransmit counters spiked. NICs show RX drop counters on mlx5. We're clearing stalled flows and will probe for bad cables/RoCE flapping.

infra-oncall: running per-host NIC diagnostics and a fabric path check. If hardware looks clean, we may roll a microcode/driver bump for the mlx5 drivers.

maya: is there an immediate mitigation from infra? can they isolate offending port or move hosts to alternate spine?

infra-oncall: isolating ports now — migrating affected nodes to alternate MPLS path. Might cause brief connection resets (~10s) but should stop retransmit storms.

sam: noted. I'll cordon node-12, drain old pods and restart the runtime after path migration.

sam: cordoned + drained node-12 -> restarted runtime container. logs show `ib_retransmit: cleared` followed by normal GPU allocation behavior.

kira: observed one container that hit `cudaLaunchKernel` errors repeatedly; restarted that pod and it recovered.

jon: routing more traffic to fallback_pool while infra finishes fabric stabilization. 70% of traffic now on fallback. system 5xx down ~65% overall.

customer-ops: informing customers A & B: "We observed networking-related packet loss affecting multi-node inference. We've routed traffic to a safe fallback and are stabilizing; estimated 2 hours for full recovery. We'll send update in 30m."

maya: good. any long-lived tasks we should do before handoff?

sam: notes — what we changed:
- set `--kvcache.cross_node=false` on serving-1
- canary traffic steering to fallback_pool (now 70%)
- cordoned/drained node-12, restarted runtime container
- infra moved affected nodes off TOR-34 and cleared ECN storms

sam: logs & snippets:
```
# sample error sequence from pod logs
[2026-03-15T17:46:12Z] rdma: retransmit detected: pkt_loss=124
[2026-03-15T17:46:14Z] kvcache: miss->rpc_fetch start
[2026-03-15T17:46:45Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T17:46:50Z] container: terminated (OOM)
```

maya: ok — I'm going to handoff to tara at 21:00 UTC (night oncall). infra, please add any follow-ups to the ticket with driver/firmware actions. customer-ops, keep the customers updated.

infra-oncall: will open infra-ticket INFRA-8342 for driver/firmware work + hardware check on TOR-34. adding NIC rx_drop counters and switch ECN config diff.

customer-ops: will send 30m update and post an incident summary for customers.

tara: taking handoff at 21:00 UTC. thanks team, I'll monitor the fallback_pool and ensure there's no regression. please ping if any new flaps.

maya: handing off — summary pinned to channel, runbook checked, all mitigations done. reassigning pager to tara. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status changed to MONITORING — mitigations applied, customer impact reduced. Next update due in 30m.
